questions.stem: At what stage do the Transport Canada emergency procedures tell the master to alert the authorities?
options: Only after the vessel has been abandoned
Only after the fire is out or the leak is fixed
Only when a passing vessel asks
Early, as soon as the vessel is assessed to be at risk
questions.explanation: The fire procedure has the master inform shore authorities once the fire has been assessed, the taking-on-water procedure has authorities notified if the vessel is at risk, and the abandon-ship procedure notifies them while preparing to abandon. Late calls cost time.

questions.stem: Which vessel must have a float-free EPIRB under NSR 2020 s. 209(1)?
options: Only a vessel on a sheltered waters voyage
Only a vessel of more than 24 m in length, whatever her voyage
A vessel on a near coastal Class 1 or unlimited voyage
Any vessel that carries a fixed VHF
questions.explanation: Section 209(1) requires a float-free EPIRB for a vessel on a near coastal voyage, Class 1 or an unlimited voyage, and for a vessel of more than 12 m on an inland voyage or a near coastal voyage, Class 2.

questions.stem: A 14 m vessel is on a near coastal voyage, Class 2. What does NSR 2020 s. 209 require of her?
options: A PLB worn by the skipper is enough
A float-free EPIRB, because she is over 12 m
Nothing, because Class 2 voyages are exempt from the rule
A DSC handheld VHF is enough on its own
questions.explanation: Section 209(1)(b) requires a float-free EPIRB on a vessel more than 12 m long on an inland voyage or a near coastal voyage, Class 2. The PLB and handheld alternatives in s. 209(3) are for vessels of 12 m or less.

questions.stem: A 7 m vessel on a near coastal voyage, Class 2 operates only in sea area A1. Which of these meets NSR 2020 s. 209(3)?
options: A waterproof DSC handheld VHF, or an EPIRB or PLB
A non-waterproof handheld VHF without DSC
A radar SART alone, kept in the cabin
A flashlight and three flares
questions.explanation: Section 209(3) lets a vessel of 12 m or less on a near coastal voyage, Class 2 carry a float-free EPIRB, a manual EPIRB, a PLB or, if under 8 m and operating only in sea area A1, a waterproof portable DSC handheld VHF. A SART and flares are not in the list.

questions.stem: After a change of owner, what must be done about a registered EPIRB?
options: Nothing, as the registry updates itself
The registration must be updated within 24 hours
The beacon must be replaced with a new one
The registration must be updated within 30 days
questions.explanation: Section 228 requires EPIRBs and PLBs to be registered with the Canadian Beacon Registry and the information updated within 30 days after a change.

questions.stem: A crew member accidentally knocks the DSC distress button and an alert is transmitted. What must be done?
options: Switch the radio off and say nothing
Wait to see if the Coast Guard calls
Cancel the alert immediately by the proper procedure
Send a second alert at once to confirm the first one was a mistake
questions.explanation: Section 244 of the Navigation Safety Regulations, 2020 requires a person who inadvertently transmits a distress alert to cancel it immediately, following the IMO guidelines for avoiding false alerts. Switching off leaves the alert standing.

questions.stem: How many pyrotechnic distress signals must a 10 m passenger-carrying vessel carry under SVR s. 410, and how many of them may be smoke signals?
options: Six, none of which may be smoke
Twelve, no more than six of them smoke
Twelve, and all of them must be smoke
Three, of which one may be smoke
questions.explanation: Over 9 m the vessel carries a watertight flashlight and twelve pyrotechnic distress signals, not more than six of which are smoke signals. Six is the figure for over 6 m to 9 m, and three for up to 6 m, and in those cases smoke signals do not count.

questions.stem: A passenger-carrying vessel is 5 m long. What visual signals does SVR s. 410 require?
options: A watertight flashlight and three non-smoke flares
Twelve pyrotechnic flares of any type
Six pyrotechnic flares of any type
A watertight flashlight only
questions.explanation: Up to 6 m, s. 410 requires a watertight flashlight and three pyrotechnic distress signals other than smoke signals. Six is for over 6 m to 9 m, and twelve for over 9 m.

questions.stem: A tour operator is about to depart from a float with a 9 m passenger vessel. What does SVR s. 402 require before departure?
options: File a float plan with the harbour master if over 12 hours
Post the passenger list on the vessel's bulletin board
Tell the passengers to call their families
Report the number aboard to a designated person ashore
questions.explanation: Section 402 requires the operator to report the number of persons on board to a designated person on shore responsible for communicating with search and rescue; in a remote area the information is left at a known location on shore.

questions.stem: A master in Canadian waters receives a distress signal from a vessel nearby. What does s. 131(1) of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 require?
options: Relay the signal and stay where you are
Call the owner for instructions first
Proceed with all speed and, if possible, tell those in distress
Proceed only if the master holds a search and rescue certificate
questions.explanation: Section 131(1) requires the master to proceed with all speed to render assistance and to inform the persons in distress or the sender if possible. A master who cannot, or who considers it unreasonable or unnecessary, enters the reason in the official log book.

questions.stem: The master of a vessel in distress finds several vessels answering. Which statement matches s. 131 of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001?
options: The master in distress must accept all offers of help equally
The master in distress may requisition answering vessels
The first vessel to arrive takes charge in all cases
Only a Coast Guard vessel may be requisitioned
questions.explanation: Section 131(3) allows the master of a vessel in distress to requisition one or more of the vessels that answer. Under s. 131(4) the others are released when they learn another vessel is complying.

questions.stem: A skipper fires a parachute flare to attract a friend's boat that is not in any danger. What does TP 14070 say?
options: It is against the law to use distress signals when not in need
It is permitted as long as the flare is more than three years old
It is permitted if it is dark
It is permitted if the Coast Guard is told afterwards
questions.explanation: TP 14070 says that using distress signals when help is not needed is against the law. An out-of-date flare or darkness does not change that.
